parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing exposure is documented: no trans-specific offence, no facility or border restriction, no police targeting, no violence record. Signals are structurally positive — decriminalisation since 1989, marriage/civil partnerships open regardless of partner sex (so a trans visitor's relationship is recognised), a constitutional discrimination ban, functioning local legislation, and a 3,000-resident society recording ~90% support for equality in consultation. Resident gaps (no gender-identity ground in the constitution, hate-stirring and sentencing provisions, no self-ID, no non-binary recognition) are climate signals at most and do not reach a visitor carrying home documents. The subnational note concerns a different territory, not this one. Deductions: trans-specific silence (no data on police practice, hate crime or services), no documented trans-specific protection operating, and open questions on facilities/custody — thin data, but extrapolating from tolerant institutions rather than hostile ones.
